item.title: Codexity Part 8: The Complete Answer Engine
item.description: The final chapter. Assemble every module into a running application. Complete source code, Docker deployment, configuration, testing, and performance tuning for the full Codexity answer engine.

item.title: Codexity Part 7: Server-Sent Events and Streaming
item.description: Implement production-grade SSE streaming in FastAPI. Handle connection drops, heartbeats, backpressure, error recovery, and the HTTP details that make streaming reliable.

item.title: Codexity Part 6: Small Model Inference with llama-cpp-python
item.description: Run a quantized 7B model locally to generate cited answers from scraped web content. Choose between Qwen, Mistral, Phi, and Llama models. Build prompts that make small models behave like large ones.

item.title: Codexity Part 5: Content Processing and Relevance Ranking
item.description: Take raw scraped text from 12 web pages and transform it into a focused context window for an LLM. Chunk text, score relevance with BM25, select the best fragments, and format them with source citations.

item.title: Codexity Part 4: Web Scraping, Proxies, and Anti-Bot Warfare
item.description: Fetch and extract content from 15 web pages concurrently. Handle JavaScript rendering with Playwright, dodge anti-bot systems, rotate proxies, and strip HTML down to clean text using readability-lxml and BeautifulSoup.

item.title: Codexity Part 3: Async Web Search with DuckDuckGo
item.description: Fire multiple search queries in parallel using DuckDuckGo's Python library and asyncio. Handle rate limiting, deduplicate results, and build a resilient search layer that does not depend on paid APIs.

item.title: Codexity Part 2: Query Rewriting with LLMs
item.description: A user types a vague question. The query rewriter transforms it into targeted search queries using a local LLM. We cover intent classification, query decomposition, and prompt engineering that actually works with small models.

item.title: Codexity Part 1: Architecture of an Answer Engine
item.description: The first chapter in a series on building a Perplexity-style answer engine from scratch in Python. We lay out the full architecture, set up the project skeleton, and understand every component before writing a single line of business logic.

item.title: Financial Prediction Report for Braiin Limited (BRAI)
item.description: Prediction: increase, Time Horizon: 21-day, Confidence: 7/10. Based on a strong bullish sentiment (75%) supported by recent news of executed contracts totaling ~US$35.93M and non-binding MoUs for an additional ~US$111.98M, alongside a key product certification (first globally certified autonomous drones for crop spraying). The company is at an early revenue stage, expecting scale from Q1 2026. However, contradictions exist: elevated RSI (77) suggests overbought conditions, and the company posts negative net income (-28.86M TTM) and negative free cash flow. The gap between gross margin (31.59%) and net margin (-39.31%) indicates severe operational inefficiency. The 21-day horizon is chosen because revenue scaling and MoU conversion are medium-term catalysts. Risks include cash burn, high valuation (P/S 30.29), and reliance on MoU conversion.
